A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAP research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE surrogate-learning experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and computational-cost measurements in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the five-PDE comparisons, supplementary evaluations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The hybrid solver/surrogate rollout, acquisition function, sampling-pattern optimization and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The expanded expected-error-reduction explanation does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Burgers, KdV, KS, incompressible and compressible Navier–Stokes equations. The time-dependent INS scenario and limited-initial-data evaluations were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Random, QbC, LCMD and SBAL, their evaluated STAP combinations, and the Bernoulli and efficient-STAP variants. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The pool and test sizes, initial training data, acquisition budgets, FNO configurations, training settings and metrics are unchanged. The multistep, 20-round and one-trajectory protocols also match across versions.

E4.justification: The sampling ablations, efficiency variants, diversity analysis, robustness evaluations and cost analysis are retained. New Appendix D.5 summarizes the existing one-trajectory experiment; its Figure 16 is v1's Figure 6, not new evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five seeds and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices and plotted uncertainty bands. No additional statistical procedure or repeated-run information is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–17 and the matched plotted results retain their numerical content. For example, Table 1 reports Burgers SBAL+STAP log RMSE of -3.674 ± 0.071 in both versions. The relocated trajectory illustration also contains identical images.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix A.2 already gives the ensemble-belief, local-error and hypothetical-retraining assumptions underlying the EER interpretation. v2 restates this reasoning in the main text, adding an explanatory standard pairwise-variance identity without changing the substantive assumptions or mathematical results.

C1.justification: The shortened abstract drops explicit claims of large-margin superiority and unusually broad mean/quantile-error improvements, retaining a general statement of benchmark effectiveness. The central contribution and the introduction's and conclusion's performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 2.3 explicitly interprets QbC as current reducible prediction error and a local approximation to EER. Section 3.2 develops this explanatory connection for selective acquisition. STAP's basic EER interpretation already existed in Appendix A.2; empirical interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, PDE solvers and parameters, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, timing information and the code-access statement are unchanged in the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Settles and Roy–McCallum, cited in the expanded EER discussion, were already cited for that connection in v1 Appendix A.2.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract, adds Section 2.3, expands Section 3.2 and adds a brief Appendix D.5 summary. It also updates the first-page publication note and makes small typography edits. Most prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The KS trajectory illustration moves from main-text Figure 6 to appendix Figure 16 with a wider arrangement. Other figures and tables are repositioned or renumbered through page reflow; their underlying displays and data are retained.

improvement.justification: Sections 2.3 and 3.2 make the acquisition rationale and its approximations easier to follow in the main text. The gain is limited because much of this reasoning already appeared in v1 Appendix A.2. The abstract loses empirical detail and an illustration moves to the appendix, but all supporting evidence remains available.
